content.thinking:
The deploy at 09:42 renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`, but the ServiceMonitor still selects `port: metrics`, so scraping finds no target—this is confirmed by actual run evidence (S1 and S2), not an unrun reading.

Checking the logs, error rates before and after look consistent with normal serving behavior, so the service itself kept working fine throughout.

So the real symptom is that shoppers saw nothing wrong while the shop's metrics simply stopped arriving, and the causal chain traces from that onset back to the port-name mismatch breaking Prometheus's target selection.

Now I'm narrowing down why: the deploy at T13 renamed the metrics port to match a platform convention, which caused the ServiceMonitor's port-name selector to match nothing. I'm ruling out the earlier deploy P1 since metrics were still arriving as late as T5's 09:41 reading, which postdates P1 and shows scraping was still functioning then.

I check flag changes too — T16 shows zero flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the incident, so I can rule those out as well. The real break comes from an inconsistency: the rename touched values-production.yaml but not deploy/scrape.yaml, which still references the old port name — so the scrape selector no longer matches any port on the service.

Since the monitoring stack treats an unmatched selector as an empty target list rather than an error, the deploy wasn't flagged at apply time and no one was paged. A missing safeguard — nothing checking that the two files agree — let this slip through review and CI undetected.

I'll keep CF-1 as the lack of a check between the port name values; AI-1 (reviewing and merging the fix with its included test) partially addresses this, but merging alone doesn't fix the running deployment since c3c36da is still live with the old port config. So there's a separate mitigation step needed: actually deploying the corrected ServiceMonitor to production once merged.

I also notice c3c36da's own branch copy of scrape.yaml shows `port: metrics`, so if that branch has its own file separate from main, it needs the same one-line fix applied there too. There's also a process concern that c3c36da isn't in main's history at all — production ran a revision not derived from main — though I'm not sure that's directly causal to the incident versus just a deployment hygiene issue worth flagging as an action item.

For the second contributing factor, I'm noting that the metrics-stopped alert was never linked to an on-call page, so nobody was notified in real time. A reasonable detection improvement would be routing a MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop to on-call so someone picks it up sooner.

For CF-3, the empty target list wasn't surfaced as an error — if the scrape config or Prometheus had flagged a selector matching zero ports, the rename would've been caught at deploy time. I'm thinking the fix should be alerting on a ServiceMonitor with zero active targets, and ideally a deploy-time check confirming the ServiceMonitor resolves to at least one endpoint after rollout, as a preventive measure.

Tracing the chain further: the scrape config selected `metrics`, but c3c36da's rename in values-production.yaml only touched that file, leaving scrape.yaml still referencing the old port name — the two were never kept in sync, and there's no evidence of why that check doesn't exist. That's where the trail goes cold, so I'll stop at that step and phrase the root cause around the mismatched port name causing an empty target list and no collected samples.

For the plain-language cause, I'm trimming it down to just state the mechanism — the rename left monitoring looking for an old port name and finding nothing — without adding claims about the shop's own serving status, since that's not part of the causal chain itself. For the still-at-risk section, I note all three replicas were confirmed running the renamed revision as of T13.1, so the mismatch was a sustained condition, not a one-off blip.

Looking at what went well, Argus correctly refused to auto-roll back an intentional change and instead surfaced the deploy diff and rollout state right after the alert fired, and Code-Fix followed up by opening a draft PR (#357) shortly after as well.

I'm checking for anything that went wrong, but the response seems to have worked as designed, so this section may end up empty.

As for assumptions, I'm noting the Prometheus target list itself wasn't directly read — the mismatch comes from the files and S1's comment, not a direct check of Prometheus's actual target state, which is a reasonable but unverified assumption.

For action items, the first is to actually deploy the corrected ServiceMonitor to production since merging to main alone won't change what's running — I need to apply the one-line port change and redeploy from whatever revision is live, and separately make the same fix in deploy/scrape.yaml on the branch.

For prevention, I should add a deploy-time check that verifies the ServiceMonitor resolves to at least one scrape target after rollout, failing the deploy otherwise — this addresses CF-2. For detection, route MetricsAbsent alerts on io-shop to the on-call pager, covering CF-3. I'm also noting a process question: revision c3c36da ran in production but isn't in main's history, which raises whether production deploys should be required to come from main.

I want to flag that nothing currently checks that the port name agrees with the scrape port name, and that AI-1's test should be sufficient to address this without needing further generalization. I also need to watch my phrasing to avoid number words — saying things like "resolves to a scrape target" or "finds no targets" instead of "at least one."

Citing the state as it stood at that instant, every replica was still running the earlier commit; I'm ruling out the possibility that the earlier deploy was the actual cause, since the shop's metrics kept flowing fine with it in place right up until the moment things changed. The logs confirm serving continued as before.

action_items.item: Once the corrected ServiceMonitor is merged, apply it in production, or redeploy the chart from a branch that carries it. Merging alone does not change what runs.
Change `port: metrics` to `port: http-metrics` in deploy/scrape.yaml on the branch revision c3c36da was deployed from: S1 shows that revision's copy still selects `port: metrics`.
Add a deploy-time check that fails a rollout when the shop's ServiceMonitor resolves to no scrape targets.
Route the MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop to the on-call pager.
Find out why revision c3c36da, which ran in production, is not in main's history, and decide whether production deploys must come from main so that fixes merged there reach what runs.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop was seen to have a problem. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped after the minute at {T5.2}, and no samples covered the minutes after that.

The metrics stopped because Prometheus's ServiceMonitor for the shop picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`, and the running configuration no longer gave any port that name: the metrics port was now named `http-metrics`. A name that matches no port leaves an empty target list, which is not raised as an error, so nothing was scraped.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731 at {P1.1}: the shop's metrics kept arriving with it in place until the minute at {T5.2}.
A feature-flag change: the flag provider showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T16.3} hour before {T16.4}.

causal_chain.step: No port was named `metrics` because the deploy of revision c3c36da at {P2.1} renamed every port to the platform's `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including the metrics port (`metrics` to `http-metrics`). As read at {T13.1}, every replica ran c3c36da.

The rename left the scrape pointing at the old name because the change touched only deploy/values-production.yaml. deploy/scrape.yaml, which has to give the same name, was left as it was at the earlier revision and still selects `port: metrics`. The record does not show why it was left out of the change.

input.cause_in_plain_words: The shop's network ports were renamed on purpose, but the monitoring system kept looking for the metrics port under its old name, so it found nothing to collect from.

contributing_factors.factor: Nothing checks that the port name in deploy/values-production.yaml matches the name the ServiceMonitor in deploy/scrape.yaml selects: the scrape file's own header says so. No check of the two against each other was seen in the rename's review.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check comparing the two files would have failed the rename before it merged, and the scrape would never have lost its target.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: When the ServiceMonitor's selector matches no port, the result is an empty target list, not an error the operator sees. Nothing at deploy time was seen confirming that the shop still had a scrape target after the rollout.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The deploy would have been flagged as soon as it rolled out, not found later by the metrics going missing.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been told the shop had gone unmonitored as soon as the alert fired, instead of the blind stretch waiting on whoever next looked.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well: Argus declined to roll back the port rename, because rolling back would have undone a change that was made on purpose and is part of a platform-wide convention.
The Investigator had read the deploy's diff and how far it had rolled out {T13.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Code-Fix opened draft pull request #357 {T20.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.

input.root_cause: Revision c3c36da renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml, but the ServiceMonitor in deploy/scrape.yaml still picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`. With no port of that name left on the Service, the shop's scrape target list was empty. The platform does not treat an empty target list as an error, so Prometheus simply stopped collecting the shop's samples.
input.still_at_risk: Revision c3c36da was still running with its metrics port named `http-metrics` while the scrape still looked for `metrics`, so the shop stayed unmonitored and a real fault in it would not show up in its metrics.
input.symptom: Shoppers saw nothing wrong, but the shop's metrics stopped arriving
